0.0.n: Written 一 in kanji, this is the first number in the counting sequence.

1.0.n: This is the number 二, not the particle に.

2.0.n: This is the number 三, not the polite ending さん used after names.

3.0.n: This is a reading of 四 used in counting; よん is another common reading.

4.0.n: This is the number 五, not the polite prefix ご.

5.0.n: ろ is the first part of ろく (六); it has no separate meaning here.

5.1.n: く completes ろく (六); it has no separate meaning here.

6.0.n: し begins しち (七); it does not mean four here.

6.1.n: ち completes しち (七); it has no separate meaning here.

7.0.n: は begins はち (八); it is not the topic particle here.

7.1.n: ち completes はち (八); it has no separate meaning here.

8.0.n: This is a reading of 九; く is another reading used in some combinations.

9.0.n: Written 十 in kanji, this number ends the counting sequence here.

0.tip: いち is the usual reading of 一 when counting.

1.tip: In this counting sequence, に is a number rather than a particle.

2.tip: さん names a number here, rather than politely addressing someone.

3.tip: Both し and よん can mean four; this sequence uses し.

4.tip: ご stands alone as a number here.

5.tip: Read ろ and く together as the single number ろく.

6.tip: しち is one number; なな is another common way to say seven.

7.tip: Read はち as one word, with は pronounced as in はな, not like the topic particle.

8.tip: Hold the final vowel longer in きゅう; the small ゅ joins き to make one sound.

9.tip: Hold the final vowel longer in じゅう; the small ゅ joins じ to make one sound.
